Many of us believe, and for good reason, that our MMR should be higher than it is. There's no accounting for a when we have a bad team. You know the kind. People saying GG before it starts. Fighting for mid. Etc... In those cases, you are guaranteed that you will lose no matter how good you are. The only thing you can do is predict a win when you have a good mix. This is why you should get extra MMR on a prediction streak. Obviously predicting 1 is a no brainer. 2 or more however... would slowly move your MMR to where you deserve to be. Thoughts?
MMR for prediction streak would balance rankings

I don't think this is a good idea.

For one thing you end up with MMR inflation (i.e. people gaining MMR where nobody else is losing an equal amount of MMR), which currently only happens when people have literally 1 MMR and lose a match.

Honestly, people eventually end up where they should be pretty much always. When they think they aren't, they're likely just in denial.

I'm not really a fan of the idea. I think Valve should implement seasons or something similar to that like in Starcraft 2 where they would make every recalibrate their MMR through 10 games again every 4 or 6 months. I think it'll be better since I know a handful of people who just played ranked to get their MMR then never touched it again but play unranked and are getting better to the point where they past their MMR level.

This isn't really a good idea.

I hate to burst your bubble but MMR is generally very accurate, you just need to think of it over a longer period of time. Yes you may lose 2-3 games to feeders and AFK's that made it 'unwinnable' but you'll probably find on average you still have the same win rate over 20 or so games etc.

The thing you need to remember is MMR is a representation of your average skill and standard of play, people can have a bad day, people can be on tilt, people can just be unlucky in some games. This will mean that they're effectively playing at a lower standard than their MMR suggests, but other times they'll play much better, and have a higher standard than the shown MMR. So when you see someone doing awfully and you think they're terrible, remember they're still at your MMR, so they are as good as you on average just having a bad game, or are drunk, or tired etc.

Also if people go 'mid or feed' then they're probably better than you mechanically, so let them have mid, their MMr will be lower than they deserver when they play mid due to the games where they don't get mid, then feed and lose. This also applies to people who are horrible flamers, flaming reduces your chances to win, but their MMR is still the same as yours (I'm assuming you're not a flamer) so despite the flaming which would reduce their MMR they are still at your level, so must be better mechanically.

Another way of thinking about this is the nicest player on your team is probably the worst as far as mechanical skill is concerned...

Overall, if you're mad that you lost, just play more and it will even itself out, if you are losing a lot, you might be on tilt yourself, so take some games out to play unranked etc before going back to ranked.

As a fantastic mid player for my potato mmr, I side with the call of if he says mid, let him take it. I will call mid but offer it to someone who also picks a mid oriented hero since I usually play Meepo mid.

Some people cry internally when I go mid Meepo, but by 10 mins they are usually happy again.

Mid is a different ball game to other lanes. Early game there is so much more finesse involved and a lot of things that can go wrong at short notice. Knowing down to 20-50hp your kill potential and death potential is critical in getting the lead.

Just last night I fucked this up vs a pudge in a lv1 man fight, he levelled up halfway through and hooked me. I didn't account for him getting the rune and being half a level ahead of me. Huge fail.

I disagree with your statement of "generally very accurate". Generally and Very are competing thoughts and combining them is the same as saying "Somewhat". Dota by design, whether accidental or on purpose, is designed to penalize the team with the worst player. It is tremendously difficult for a "Great" player to carry a "Terrible" player. There needs to be a mechanism to shield average from terrible players. Terrible players, abandon, flame, feed. There should be harsher penalties and moderation for them or a way for those who don't to stay ahead/away of the ones that do.

No, i meant that for a general player it is very accurate, only players who abuse the calibration system, accounts or smurf are exceptions.

If someone has the same mmr as you then on average they are as good as you. That's it, that's what mmr tells you. There's no arguing with this. But they might be on tilt, so for that game play worse than their average.

The penalties already are pretty harsh, an abandon counts worse than a report already, feeding because you play bad, out are underfarmed etc I'd not an offence.

Mmr loss is the penalty for shit play, it's there already.

Over the course of a lot of games the impact of feeders etc level out, that's why mmr is accurate.

Also how on earth do you lose because of flame? If that was truly the case then you could have muted them and won, surely?

So I'm that case the loss is your fault, you should have muted and gg.

Stop getting caught up with X is feeding BS, there are always ways YOU could have done better, you could have ganked mid to help them get back their lane, rather than blame them.

You could stack for your carry, rather than moan they have no farm.

You can buy wards or dust even if you're not a support.

There is ALWAYS more you could have done. Stop blaming, stop wanting the system to change, stop thinking there's such a thing as an unwinnable game.

The game came out yesterday, and there are some things the developers need to fix or patch up, but if they do this might be a pretty fun game.  

  1. The looks of the game is really eye-pleasing, although there were/are times when I have to hover over buildings just to know what they are good for.
  2. You can spend your energy either on clicking, which gives you money/dollars or on studying at school so that you'll be able to get a better paying job (more $/click)
  3. The energy system kind of bothers be to be honest, and the fact that you can buy more energy with Kong Kredits bothers me even more. You have 5 free energy refills when you start the game, I don't know if you'll get more the next day though, the waiting for the energy bar to be full is about 3 hours. - it also gives you a sense of strategy. Make more money or spend your hard earned money to study at school and get a better job (more $/click)
  4. The stock system seems interesting enough, if you have the patience for it and you make the right moves you can make more out of your money than the amount you've put in. I didn't experience yet with this that much, I'm merely just exploring the game.
  5. The banking system of the game is where your offline production will come from, with a difference that it also produces money when you're online, think of it more like an investment system, where you buy bonds and you get income from it ($/minute) - You also have to manually collect them when they get full, so you can only accumulate that much money while online or offline, you can, of course, upgrade the storage amount.
  6. A down point is, that the game seems to be an 'always online' type of game, where if you lose your internet connection for more than a few seconds, it'll disconnect you and you may have lost a fragment of the progress you've made while your internet disconnected. It happened to me, lost half a month's (in-game time) money.

 

These are my thoughts about the game for now. It is definitely worth a look at, and if the issues get fixed, I'm sure the game will get a higher rating than it already has (3.4 - with 360 ratings). I'll definitely be playing it just to explore all of its systems.

 

I hope you'll enjoy the game! Keep on clickin'!
